implementation_notes: The C version of the smell is often the strongest form, because C is a language-agnostic substrate that invites the belief that every problem — text processing, concurrency, GUI, database access — is best served by writing it in C. The concrete symptom in a C codebase is a single system whose data structures, string handling, threading model and I/O strategy are all settled because that is what the C standard provides, with no requirement ever recorded. The remedy is the same process change, plus the practical one of checking whether the standard library (and POSIX) already covers the requirement before writing C for it.
idiom_name: one library/standard (or C itself) applied to every problem shape
pitfalls: Writing a bespoke implementation of something the standard library or POSIX already provides is the most common C Golden Hammer and is invisible in review because the code looks reasonable.
Memory management everywhere when a managed runtime would remove it is a design choice made by default.
An in-house framework nobody outside the team can learn is a capability the team has accidentally made itself dependent on.
